requirements.quote:
Once the GOAWAY is sent, the sender will ignore frames sent on
   streams initiated by the receiver if the stream has an identifier
   higher than the included last stream identifier.  Receivers of a
requirements.condition: After an endpoint sends a GOAWAY frame and receives a frame on a receiver-initiated stream whose identifier exceeds the included last stream identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the frame, except where connection-state processing requirements later in this chunk apply.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send frames on receiver-initiated streams above the advertised identifier after GOAWAY and observe whether ordinary stream processing occurs.

requirements.quote:
higher than the included last stream identifier.  Receivers of a
   GOAWAY frame MUST NOT open additional streams on the connection,
   although a new connection can be established for new streams.
requirements.condition: After receiving a GOAWAY frame on a connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Open any additional stream on that connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A stateful test can receive GOAWAY and then verify that the implementation does not initiate another stream on the same connection.

requirements.quote:
If the receiver of the GOAWAY has sent data on streams with a higher
   stream identifier than what is indicated in the GOAWAY frame, those
   streams are not or will not be processed.  The receiver of the GOAWAY
requirements.condition: The receiver of GOAWAY sent data on a stream whose identifier is higher than the last stream identifier in GOAWAY.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the stream as not processed or as one that will not be processed by the GOAWAY sender.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assume that the GOAWAY sender processed or will process the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can track affected streams and verify the implementation's processing/retry classification after receiving GOAWAY.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints SHOULD always send a GOAWAY frame before closing a
   connection so that the remote peer can know whether a stream has been
   partially processed or not.  For example, if an HTTP client sends a
requirements.condition: An endpoint is about to close a connection, absent a justified exception such as a misbehaving peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a GOAWAY frame before closing the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection-shutdown test can observe whether GOAWAY precedes closure.

requirements.quote:
connection; a receiver of a GOAWAY that has no more use for the
   connection SHOULD still send a GOAWAY frame before terminating the
   connection.
requirements.condition: A GOAWAY receiver has no more use for the connection and is going to terminate it.
requirements.required_behavior: Send its own GOAWAY frame before terminating the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A bidirectional shutdown test can verify that the receiver transmits GOAWAY before terminating.

requirements.condition: Encoding or parsing a GOAWAY frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and recognize the 8-bit Type field with the fixed value 0x07.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode a GOAWAY frame with a different type value.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized frame type field can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: Unused Flags (8),
requirements.condition: Encoding or parsing a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the flags field as an 8-bit unused field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Interpret any flag bit as a GOAWAY-defined flag.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser or serializer test can inspect the flags field and verify that no GOAWAY-specific flags are exposed.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31) = 0,
requirements.condition: Encoding a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 31-bit Stream Identifier field as 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The fixed field value is directly observable in serialized frames.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Last-Stream-ID (31),
     Error Code (32),
     Additional Debug Data (..),
requirements.condition: Encoding or parsing a GOAWAY frame payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a 1-bit reserved field, a 31-bit Last-Stream-ID, a 32-bit Error Code, and a variable-length Additional Debug Data field in that order.
requirements.why_checkable: Binary layout tests can verify field widths and ordering.

requirements.quote: The GOAWAY frame does not define any flags.
requirements.condition: Processing the flags field of a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat all flag bits as undefined for GOAWAY.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign GOAWAY-specific semantics to any flag bit.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's parser behavior can be tested with every flag bit set.

requirements.quote: The GOAWAY frame applies to the connection, not a specific stream.
requirements.condition: Processing a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the frame to the connection rather than to an individual stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply GOAWAY solely as a stream-specific operation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can observe whether GOAWAY changes connection-level stream-admission and shutdown state.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST treat a GOAWAY frame with a stream identifier other
   than 0x00 as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: A GOAWAY frame has a stream identifier other than 0x00.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept or process the frame as a valid GOAWAY.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the condition as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed frame with a nonzero stream identifier can be injected and the resulting connection error code observed.

requirements.quote:
The last stream identifier in the GOAWAY frame contains the highest-
   numbered stream identifier for which the sender of the GOAWAY frame
   might have taken some action on or might yet take action on.  All
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends or interprets a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use Last-Stream-ID as the highest-numbered stream on which the sender might have acted or might yet act.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream-processing history can be compared with the value encoded in or interpreted from GOAWAY.

requirements.quote:
streams up to and including the identified stream might have been
   processed in some way.  The last stream identifier can be set to 0 if
   no streams were processed.
requirements.condition: No streams were processed before sending GOAWAY.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit Last-Stream-ID to be set to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: A shutdown test with no processed streams can inspect whether a zero Last-Stream-ID is supported.

requirements.quote:
If a connection terminates without a GOAWAY frame, the last stream
   identifier is effectively the highest possible stream identifier.
requirements.condition: A connection terminates without a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the effective last stream identifier as the highest possible stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: A client-side termination test can inspect how outstanding streams are classified when no GOAWAY was received.

requirements.quote:
On streams with lower- or equal-numbered identifiers that were not
   closed completely prior to the connection being closed, reattempting
   requests, transactions, or any protocol activity is not possible,
   except for idempotent actions like HTTP GET, PUT, or DELETE.  Any
requirements.condition: A stream identifier is lower than or equal to Last-Stream-ID and the stream was not completely closed before connection closure.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow reattempt only for idempotent actions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reattempt non-idempotent requests, transactions, or protocol activity on the assumption that they were unprocessed.
requirements.why_checkable: Retry logic can be tested using closed incomplete streams carrying idempotent and non-idempotent operations.

requirements.quote:
except for idempotent actions like HTTP GET, PUT, or DELETE.  Any
   protocol activity that uses higher-numbered streams can be safely
   retried using a new connection.
requirements.condition: Protocol activity used a stream numbered higher than the Last-Stream-ID in GOAWAY.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit that activity to be retried using a new connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Retry classification can be inspected for streams above the advertised boundary.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MAY send multiple GOAWAY frames if circumstances change.
requirements.condition: Circumstances change after an endpoint has sent a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the endpoint to send additional GOAWAY frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can verify that a second GOAWAY is accepted and emitted when configured.

requirements.quote:
identifier from the last GOAWAY frame received indicates which
   streams could have been acted upon.  Endpoints MUST NOT increase the
   value they send in the last stream identifier, since the peers might
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a subsequent GOAWAY frame on the same connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the new Last-Stream-ID less than or equal to the value previously sent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Increase the Last-Stream-ID value relative to an earlier GOAWAY.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of emitted GOAWAY frames can be checked for monotonically nonincreasing Last-Stream-ID values.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2.  A server that is attempting to gracefully shut down a
   connection SHOULD send an initial GOAWAY frame with the last stream
   identifier set to 2^31-1 and a NO_ERROR code.  This signals to the
requirements.condition: A server is attempting to gracefully shut down a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Send an initial GOAWAY with Last-Stream-ID set to 2^31-1 and error code NO_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: The server's first GOAWAY during graceful shutdown can be inspected for both fixed values.

requirements.quote:

   creation (at least one round-trip time), the server MAY send another
   GOAWAY frame with an updated last stream identifier.  This ensures
requirements.condition: A server has sent the initial graceful-shutdown GOAWAY and elects to send another GOAWAY with an updated Last-Stream-ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Wait at least one round-trip time for in-flight stream creation before sending the subsequent GOAWAY.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the updated GOAWAY before at least one round-trip time has elapsed.
requirements.why_checkable: An instrumented timing test can measure the interval between the initial and updated GOAWAY frames.

requirements.quote:
After sending a GOAWAY frame, the sender can discard frames for
   streams initiated by the receiver with identifiers higher than the
   identified last stream.  However, any frames that alter connection
   state cannot be completely ignored.  For instance, HEADERS,
requirements.condition: After sending GOAWAY, a frame for a receiver-initiated stream above Last-Stream-ID would alter connection state.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform the connection-state processing required by the frame even if its stream-level effects are discarded.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can send connection-state-altering frames above the boundary and inspect shared connection state afterward.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE, and CONTINUATION frames MUST be minimally processed to
   ensure that the state maintained for field section compression is
   consistent (see Section 4.3); similarly, DATA frames MUST be counted
requirements.condition: After GOAWAY, a HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION frame arrives on a receiver-initiated stream above Last-Stream-ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Minimally process the frame sufficiently to keep field-section compression state consistent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Completely discard the frame without updating field-section compression state.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted header-block sequence can verify that compression state remains synchronized despite ignored stream-level activity.

requirements.quote:
consistent (see Section 4.3); similarly, DATA frames MUST be counted
   toward the connection flow-control window.  Failure to process these
   frames can cause flow control or field section compression state to
requirements.condition: After GOAWAY, a DATA frame arrives, including on a receiver-initiated stream above Last-Stream-ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Count the DATA frame toward the connection flow-control window.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discard the DATA frame without accounting for its connection-level flow-control consumption.
requirements.why_checkable: A flow-control test can send DATA after GOAWAY and verify the resulting connection-window accounting.
